confirm.text: Nothing to report. The "What did we observe?" multi-select appears only on air job and OWL After Action Review forms, and none were submitted on 11/01 — every air job on the Permian board was either ON STANDBY or RESCHEDULED. No form filed on this day carried a multi-select field of any kind, so there is no selection to confirm and no repeat-offender pattern to track for Sunday.
Air jobs: none were assigned on 11/01. All SM Energy NORM and maintenance air job rows and all four XTO rows were ON STANDBY or RESCHEDULED, so no air job documentation was due.
Confined space: both SM Energy MONEY GRAHAM CTB confined space rows (trailer 148) were ON STANDBY. Nothing was due.
Field service: no field service assignments on either board for 11/01.
Supervision — shifts with no daily inspection form received. Full-time employees first:

Dennis Easley — SM Energy, COLD SNACK FED COM 214H, workover supervision, days, ticket 102667, board AT# 151. No form of any kind was received from Easley on 11/01. The board shows him WORKING, lodging at Carlsbad. He filed on 10/31 for a different well, so he is an active filer. This is the clearest gap of the day.

Michael Ellis — Comstock, ELLIOT #1, production supervision, nights, board AT# 142. No daily inspection form received for the night shift. Josh Blassingame covered the day shift on the same row and filed.
Don Quisenberry 1099 — Comstock, SEABURGS PAD, drillout supervision, nights, board AT# 138. No daily received. Allen White covered days on the same row and filed.
Steve Henson 1099 (days) and Cleveland Broughton 1099 (nights) — Comstock, KRETZSCHMAR PBH 1H, flowback supervision, ticket 102366, board AT# 130. No daily received from either shift.

On the 1099 names above, it is still not established whether every contractor is set up to file in StreetSmart at all, so a form that was never expected is not a form that is missing. One further caveat applies to all four night-shift absences: a night shift beginning the evening of 11/01 can submit after midnight Central, and this review ran at roughly 10 PM Central, so a late daily from Ellis, Quisenberry or Broughton would not yet be visible. Benjamin Boutte filed his night daily at 6:34 PM, so evening filing does happen, but the window is not closed.
Satisfied in ways that might look wrong at a glance — please do not chase these:

Marcos Morales 1099, Ovintiv, H&P 551, UL CATHEDRAL 36, supervision, job 36270_1, ticket 102515, board AT# N/A. He filed no H2S daily for 11/01, but the job record shows no shift was worked that day. The log reads Start Job Daily 10/31 06:15 AM, Pause Job 10/31 06:29 PM, then End This Job and Upload Ticket 11/01 06:21 PM with no intervening daily start. Suspended Time is recorded as 1d:12h:34m. On that reading 11/01 was a close-out only, and a daily inspection form was not due. Confirm if you want it treated otherwise.
Brey Rasco (days) and Benjamin Boutte 1099 (nights) both filed for SM Energy JUNIOR MINT 156H, ticket 102668 — both shifts on that row are covered.

Larry Taylor filed both of his rig up job records, 36414 for Comstock NEYLAND ML 1H at Patterson 904 and 36413 for Comstock CIRCLE M ALLOC B 2H. Both were properly ENDED with no suspension, and both rows carry AT# N/A, so no trailer forms were due for either.

Trailer forms — a question rather than an assertion. Five trailers appear on 11/01 live assignment rows: 130, 138 and 142 on the ArkLaTex board and 503 and 151 on the Permian board. No Trailer Inspection Form and no Trailer Readiness Form was received for any of those five. The only two trailer forms submitted on the day were Trailer Inspection Forms for 505 (Hutt, Kilgore shop) and 504 (Drake, Mentone), and neither trailer appears as an AT# on any 11/01 manned row. Before this is treated as five gaps: the standing two-inspections-plus-one-readiness daily requirement is written against air jobs, and every row above is a supervision assignment with the trailer already sitting on location. Whether that requirement extends to supervision rows needs your confirmation. If it does, 11/01 was short fifteen submissions; if it does not, nothing is missing here. doc.text: Bottle Hydro Dates and cascade pressures

Benjamin Boutte 1099, Junior Mint, trailer 503 per the board — cascade recorded as "2100", Bottle Hydro Dates left blank. Re-read from the PDF, the text runs straight from "2100 Pressure on Cascade System" to "Bottle Hydro Dates" with no value in between. Because AT# 503 names a trailer, this is a valid finding. This is a repeat: Boutte was flagged on 09/26 for leaving both the hydro dates and the cascade pressure blank with a trailer on location. The cascade pressure is filled in this time; the hydro dates are not.
Brey Rasco, Junior Mint, same trailer 503 — cascade recorded as "2200x6", Bottle Hydro Dates left blank. Same reading, same conclusion: a valid finding because the board names a trailer.

Allen White, Seaburgs Pad, trailer 138 — clean. Cascade "8@2400" and hydro "6@1-23 1@122 1@3-23" are both populated and both complete. The middle entry "1@122" is missing a separator where the others have one; that is a typing question, not a missing value, and nothing needs chasing unless you want the entry tidied.

Josh Blassingame, Elliot #1, trailer 142 — hydro dates recorded as "1-23". The cascade field reads "All 8 bottles full", which describes the bottles rather than recording a pressure. Every other cascade entry on the day is numeric. Worth asking him for the psi figure.

Exempt because the board AT# is exactly N/A: Larry Taylor's two rig up jobs (Neyland ML 1H and Circle M Alloc B 2H) and Marcos Morales's Ovintiv supervision job. Blank hydro and cascade fields on those forms are expected and are not counted against anyone.
Photos not taken on the day being verified

Josh Blassingame, Elliot #1 — the ELSA photo set, the Loud Alarm Position photo set and the fire extinguisher tag photo all carry a capture stamp of 08/12/2021 10:02 AM. Both 4 Gas photos carry 10/22/2026 07:32 AM. Everything else on his form is 11/01/2026.
Allen White, Seaburgs Pad — the ELSA photos and the Loud Alarm Position photos carry the same 08/12/2021 10:02 AM stamp. Everything else is 11/01/2026.

That identical 08/12/2021 10:02 AM timestamp appearing on two different technicians' forms at two different locations on the same day suggests a shared stale photo set carried in the app rather than two independent oversights. This is the persistent ELSA and Loud Alarm problem, and it may be worth fixing at the app or template level rather than one technician at a time.

Larry Taylor, Circle M Alloc B 2H rig up (job 36413) — Loud Ass Alarm Placement stamped 02/10/2026 07:50 PM; Loud Ass Alarm Destination and Source, ELSA Placement, ELSA Pressure Gauge and the Skid Date photo all stamped 10/27/2026 09:19 AM.
Larry Taylor, Neyland ML 1H rig up (job 36414) — Skid Date photo stamped 02/10/2026 07:50 PM.

clean.text: Marcos Morales 1099 filed the cleanest record of the day — the Ovintiv UL CATHEDRAL 36 supervision close-out (job 36270_1), with a coherent multi-day start, pause and end sequence across 10/30 to 11/01, daily work summaries on both worked days and tube counts recorded; the only mark against it is the blank ticket field noted above. Allen White's H2S daily for Seaburgs Pad is clean on every data field, including a complete and properly formatted cascade and hydro entry, with only the stale ELSA and Loud Alarm photos counting against it. Michael Hutt's and Dawson Drake's Trailer Inspection Forms are both photographically complete and same-day throughout; the FR answer is the only issue on either. Larry Taylor's two rig up jobs were both correctly started and ended with full equipment checklists and no suspension irregularities.

Trailer forms of both kinds, and the equipment sections of the H2S daily, are photo-based. A defect visible only in a photograph would not surface in this review — I can read that a photo exists and when it was captured, but not what it shows. Fire extinguisher inspection and expiration dates, first aid kit dates and 4-gas calibration dates exist only inside images, never as text, so none of them can be verified here. One related note: on both Benjamin Boutte's and Brey Rasco's dailies, the "Picture of both fire extinguisher tags" label appears with no capture entry in front of it, where every other photo field on those forms has one. That may mean no photo was attached, or it may be an extraction artifact — it needs a look at the forms in StreetSmart to tell which.

A second limitation specific to tonight: this review ran at about 10 PM Central, so any submission filed late on Sunday night or arriving Monday morning for Sunday's work is not in it. That bears most on the four night-shift dailies listed as not received.

9 of 9 submissions read. The job board was available — Blake Walton's 11/1/2026 Ark-La-Tex & Permian Basin Job & Rental Boards, received 11:00 AM Central, and the "11-1 DRAFT" sheet was used from both the ArkLaTex and Permian Basin November workbooks. 52 manned board rows were checked across the two boards, of which 12 were live assignments covering 18 technician-shifts once ON STANDBY, RESCHEDULED, DAYS OFF, MOBILIZING, WTX SUPPORT and leave rows were removed.
